title: Ratios and qualifications
description: How many staff you need for the children in the room, and which qualifications count. Based on section 3 of the EYFS statutory framework.

questions.prompt: For children aged under two, what is the minimum staffing ratio?

options.text: At least one member of staff for every three children

questions.explanation: For children aged under two there must be at least one member of staff for every three children. At least one member of staff must hold an approved level 3 qualification and be suitably experienced in working with children under two.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: For children aged two, what is the minimum staffing ratio?

options.text: At least one member of staff for every five children

questions.explanation: For children aged two there must be at least one member of staff for every five children. At least one member of staff must hold an approved level 3 qualification, and at least half of all other staff must hold an approved level 2 qualification.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Anyone aged 16 can be counted in the ratios. True or false?
questions.explanation: False. Providers must not include anyone aged under 17 in ratios, except apprentices, who may be included from the age of 16. Nobody aged under 17 may care for children unsupervised at any time.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: What qualification must the manager of a setting on the early years register hold?

options.text: An approved qualification at level 3 or above
No qualification, if they have two years’ experience

questions.explanation: In settings on the early years register, the manager must hold an approved qualification at level 3 or above, and at least half of all other staff must hold at least an approved level 2 qualification.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: How close must staff be to the children?

options.text: Children must usually be within sight and hearing of staff, and always within sight or hearing
Children can be out of sight and hearing for short periods
Staff only need to be in the building
Staff only need to see children during meals

questions.explanation: Children must usually be within sight and hearing of staff and always within sight or hearing. Paragraph 3.70 applies when children are eating.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: The ratio requirements apply to the total number of staff available to work directly with children across the whole provision, not just each room. True or false?
questions.explanation: True. The ratio requirements apply to the total number of staff available to work directly with children across the whole provision, not just each room. Ofsted may decide that a higher staff to child ratio is needed to keep children safe.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Staff with an Early Years Educator qualification must also have a suitable level 2 qualification in English to count in the ratios at level 3. True or false?
questions.explanation: True. To count within the ratios at level 3, staff holding an Early Years Educator qualification, and those approved at level 3 through the experience-based route, must also have achieved a suitable level 2 qualification in English.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: In the baby room there are nine children under two. Two members of staff are in the room. Kai, aged 15, is on a work experience week and offers to help so the ratio looks fine.

choices.text: Do not count Kai in the ratios, and tell your manager that a third member of staff is needed
choices.feedback: Right. Nine children under two need at least three staff, and nobody aged under 17 can be counted in the ratios (apprentices from 16 are the exception).

choices.text: Count Kai, because they are helping
choices.feedback: People aged under 17 cannot be counted in the ratios.

choices.text: Count Kai, but only while the manager is out of the room
choices.feedback: There is no exception like this. Kai cannot be counted.

questions.explanation: Under twos need at least one member of staff for every three children, so nine children need at least three staff. Providers must not include anyone aged under 17 in ratios, except apprentices who may be included from the age of 16.
